image_prompt.text: Downtown skyscrapers of 15 to 50+ floors with glass curtain wall facades, patterned window grids and antenna spikes on top, standing as the dominant tall structures visible from across the city so you always know where downtown is

A street grid threading the whole city so movement has an obvious grain: narrow one-way streets, two-way streets and wider multi-lane avenues, all with painted lane dividers, flanked by slightly raised curbed sidewalks and meeting at crosswalk-striped intersections

Built-up ground as a dense city block grid of mid-rise buildings of 3 to 10 floors rather than scattered individual buildings, varied between brick, concrete and glass facades in a muted 2000s urban palette of grays, browns and blues, with visible window patterns and doors on the ground floor and no visible interiors
Composed street-level views looking down the avenues, framed by neon-lit facades and receding towers, built to look good from a specific vantage point
Glowing neon signs and billboards on the building facades in bright pink, cyan, red and yellow, concentrated on the lower floors and rooftops, with some mounted vertically along the building edges

Street light poles lining the streets and sidewalks, mixed between warm orange sodium-vapour and cool white LED, some tall enough to illuminate the roadway and some decorative at pedestrian level, with traffic light poles at the intersections

notes: No genre: the prompt describes a place and an aesthetic with no gameplay, players, scoring or objective, so no-genre.md was loaded rather than inventing a genre to escape it.

would have asked: Sounds like an explorable place — a dense 2000s New York-style block grid of mid-rise buildings, downtown glass towers as the landmark you navigate by, streets and sidewalks threading between them, and composed neon-lit street views. All defaults on the routing axes, so it is a single-pass exterior build. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: confirming the city is walked through at street level rather than only orbited by a camera — sidewalks are described as pedestrian paths and the intersections have crosswalks, but no player is ever mentioned. Taken as walkable, so no SET; if nothing ever walks on it this should be re-emitted as ["P0", "SET"].

would have asked: the prompt says buildings have no visible interiors, so building-interior was deliberately left off and nothing routes P3 — say the word if any lobby or ground-floor shop should actually be enterable.

would have asked: Anything else you want in the space? (step 5 open question, unanswered — no additions beyond what the prompt already states; in particular no crowds or traffic were requested, so npc-population was not applied)

Close call on structure-criticality: a road grid where every intersection has to connect could be read as must-be-valid (P6), but no game depends on the topology here, so it stays dressed and routes P0.
Stated quantities that could not ride in count because they are ranges rather than single numbers, kept in text instead: mid-rise buildings of 3-10 floors, skyscrapers of 15-50+ floors.

The prompt asks for exposed generator attributes — city block count, street width, building height range, skyscraper density, neon intensity, street light colour (orange/white/mixed), one-way vs two-way street mix, sidewalk width — and asks that increasing scale add more city blocks with different street configurations. No option or field carries these, so they are recorded here.
